doc: The framework-neutral IO pair, and the composed error block. These carriers name no framework: `input.value` / `output.value` is what a great many instrumentations write when they write anything, which is why they are a dialect of their own rather than any one framework's file.

carriers.doc: Accumulated framework state that happens to contain messages - an agent's scratchpad, a chain's running result. Ordered, re-lists itself, and says nothing about multiplicity: the same tool call appears at two positions while describing one call. Still the span's output, which is why direction cannot be derived from being an emission.
The same shape on the receiving side: state handed to the span.
A single message handed to the span.
A message list handed to the span.

The error built from a span's exception fields. The span produced it, it is not a re-send, and it has no position in any payload - it is composed rather than read, which is why it states no sequence order.

messages.doc: The generic input carrier, read only if no dialect recognised the span. `json_or_string` because these are documented as *any* JSON and a producer whose input is bare text writes exactly that - requiring JSON dropped every such answer silently.
One dialect's stand-in for that carrier, read in the same stage and only where the carrier it stands in for is absent - it is the same datum under another name, not a second one.
The same dialect's stand-in on the producing side.
The generic output carrier. Last, because the retired stage read it last and the order is observable.
